rca.title: A2-D01: approved-leave rejection refunded the actor instead of requester (Issue #4)
whys: Requester balance was not restored on approved rejection.
The refund lookup selected the authenticated acting employee.
The actor can be the approver while request.employee_id is a different employee.
Correct status alone did not establish the balance-owner invariant.
A status-only test cannot detect the cross-user credit; this last point is a test-design inference, not a claim about past human practice.
rca.control: Correction 546cb620 uses the request owner and stored available/carry split. Distinct requester/actor/outsider snapshots and exact debit/refund/repeat controls now pass; source-backed observed chain, no invented organizational cause.

rca.title: A2-D03: submission used raw carry balance instead of policy cap (Issue #6)
whys: Leave exceeding effective entitlement was accepted.
The submission calculation used raw stored carry-forward.
Stored carry can be five while current policy cap is one.
Submission and existing policy calculation could diverge.
An under-cap fixture cannot distinguish these rules; this is a logical boundary-testing inference.
rca.control: Correction 546cb620 applies the existing carry policy at submission; P3 current-policy approval checks prevent a later over-cap grant. Independent capped/no-carry/forecast/expiry fixtures assert rejection and unchanged funds; no new arbitrary policy is invented.
